five_minute_explanation: Players and the GM build the world and story together.
The fiction determines when mechanics are used, and mechanical results must change the fiction.
Players roll two d12s: a Hope Die and a Fear Die.
A roll determines both success or failure and whether Hope or Fear shapes what follows.
There is no rigid initiative by default; attention moves through an organic spotlight.
Say what your character wants and how they attempt it; the GM calls for a roll only when uncertainty and consequences matter.
Most player action rolls use two d12s. Add the chosen trait and any paid Experience bonuses, then compare the total with Difficulty.
The higher Duality Die determines Hope or Fear, while matching dice produce a Critical Success.
Combat uses a flexible spotlight instead of default initiative; pass attention fairly and let the fiction determine who acts next.
minimum_materials: A character sheet and character guide for each player.
Two visually distinct d12s per player, designated Hope and Fear.
Other polyhedral dice used by weapons, abilities, healing, adversaries, and features: commonly d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and sometimes d20.
A way to track Hope, Fear, Stress, Hit Points, Armor Slots, usage limits, and countdowns.
Core cards or digital equivalents for class, subclass, ancestry, community, and domain abilities.

agenda.activity: Review concept, tone, safety, and the difference between Hope/Fear and success/failure.
Choose pregenerated PCs or finish Level 1 characters and connections.
Run a social or exploration scene with one low-stakes action roll, one Experience use, and Help an Ally.
Run a conflict that demonstrates spotlight movement, an adversary attack, damage thresholds, Armor Slots, and a condition.
Take a short rest and demonstrate downtime and GM Fear gain.
Resolve a final obstacle with a countdown or Tag Team Roll.
Debrief what was fun or confusing and record any agreed table rulings.

teaching_order: Duality Dice and the five outcomes.

game_at_a_glance.genre: Collaborative heroic fantasy tabletop roleplaying game with narrative-first play and long-term character progression.
central_ideas: Players and the GM build the world and story together.
The fiction determines when mechanics are used, and mechanical results must change the fiction.
Players roll two d12s: a Hope Die and a Fear Die.
A roll determines both success or failure and whether Hope or Fear shapes what follows.
There is no rigid initiative by default; attention moves through an organic spotlight.
game_at_a_glance.winning: There is no single competitive victory condition. The table aims to create an enjoyable, coherent story and discover what happens through play.

essential: A character sheet and character guide for each player.
Two visually distinct d12s per player, designated Hope and Fear.
Other polyhedral dice used by weapons, abilities, healing, adversaries, and features: commonly d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and sometimes d20.
A way to track Hope, Fear, Stress, Hit Points, Armor Slots, usage limits, and countdowns.
Core cards or digital equivalents for class, subclass, ancestry, community, and domain abilities.
optional: Miniatures, tokens, terrain, or a map.
A spotlight tracker for groups that want more visible action-sharing.
Official quickstart pregenerated characters and adventure.
Demiplane or another authorized digital toolset.
what_you_need.recommended_first_game: Use the official Sablewood Messengers Quickstart Adventure with pregenerated characters before building a full campaign.

players: Describe what their characters think, say, and do.
Ask questions about the scene before committing to action.
Choose how to pursue goals and accept that danger and complications move the story.
Manage Hope, Stress, Hit Points, Armor Slots, equipment, Experiences, and cards.
Contribute setting details when invited and help spotlight other players.
Narrate or co-narrate successes when appropriate.
game_master: Frame scenes and portray the world, NPCs, adversaries, and environments.
Tell players what their characters can easily perceive without requiring unnecessary rolls.
Call for a roll only when the outcome is uncertain and both success and failure are interesting.
Choose or approve the relevant trait and set Difficulty when a rule does not provide it.
State stakes, possible consequences, and unavoidable costs before the roll.
Use GM moves and Fear to keep events changing.
Move the spotlight fairly and maintain a safe, collaborative table.
shared_responsibility: Begin with the fiction, use mechanics, then return to the fiction.
Build on each other's ideas rather than protecting a prewritten outcome.
Make rulings that support the agreed tone and logic of the world.
Treat safety boundaries as living agreements that can be updated at any time.

session_zero.goal: Agree on the kind of game everyone is consenting to play before long-term play begins.
recommended_topics: Concept: What is the campaign about?
Aim: What are the characters expected to pursue and what kind of play should be emphasized?
Tone: Heroic, tragic, cozy, horror-leaning, comedic, political, romantic, or another agreed mixture.
Safety: Lines, veils, an X-card or equivalent pause/edit tool, and an open-door policy.
Campaign frame or setting assumptions.
Character creation boundaries and allowed options.
How much player-authored worldbuilding everyone enjoys.
Expected session length, attendance, scheduling, and communication.
PvP, secrets, romance, character death, and intra-party conflict.
Accessibility needs and any adjustments to cards, dice, visual trackers, audio, or pacing.

safety_tools.lines: Content that does not appear in the game.
safety_tools.veils: Content that may exist but is not described in detail or played on-screen.
safety_tools.x_card: A way for anyone to pause and remove or revise uncomfortable content without needing to justify the request.

cats.aim: What the group is trying to do during play.
cats.tone: The intended emotional and genre experience.
cats.safety: Boundaries and tools used to protect everyone.

steps.name: Choose class and subclass
instructions: Choose one of the nine Core Set classes.
Take the class sheet and guide.
Choose one of that class's two subclasses and take its foundation card.
Resolve any choices required by the class or subclass.

steps.name: Choose heritage
instructions: Choose an ancestry, which grants two ancestry features.
Choose a community, which grants one community feature.
A mixed ancestry uses the first-listed feature of one ancestry and the second-listed feature of another.

steps.name: Assign traits
instructions: Assign +2, +1, +1, +0, +0, and -1 across the six traits in any order.
Traits influence action and reaction rolls, and weapons or spells specify which trait they use.

steps.name: Record starting information
instructions: Record Level 1.
Copy starting Evasion and starting Hit Points from the class sheet.
Every PC begins with 6 Stress slots.
Every PC begins with 2 Hope.

steps.name: Choose starting equipment
instructions: Choose either one two-handed primary weapon or a one-handed primary plus a one-handed secondary weapon.
Start with Proficiency 1 and calculate weapon damage using one weapon damage die plus its listed modifier.
Choose Tier 1 armor and add Level 1 to its base Major and Severe thresholds.
Record its Armor Score as available Armor Slots, after any permanent adjustments.
Add a torch, 50 feet of rope, basic supplies, and 1 handful of gold.
Choose either a Minor Health Potion or Minor Stamina Potion.
Add the class-specific starting item and any GM-approved personal items.

steps.name: Create background
instructions: Answer or replace the background prompts in the class guide.
Background is primarily narrative, but it helps the GM prepare relevant people, places, problems, and hooks.

steps.name: Create Experiences
instructions: Write two specific Experiences, each at +2.
An Experience should describe a useful background, specialty, identity, training, or recurring capability.
Avoid universally applicable phrases and avoid wording that grants a new supernatural power or rules immunity.

steps.name: Choose domain cards
instructions: Choose two Level 1 cards from the class's two domains.
They may come one from each domain or both from the same domain.
Both begin in the active loadout.

steps.name: Create connections
instructions: Introduce characters to one another.
Use class-guide connection prompts or invent your own.
Each player may accept, revise, or reject any proposed connection.
It is acceptable for some relationships to be discovered during play.

Agility.summary: Speed, balance, mobility, and nimble reactions.

Strength.summary: Raw power, bodily endurance, and force.

Finesse.summary: Accuracy, stealth, delicate control, and technical precision.

Instinct.summary: Awareness, intuition, wilderness sense, and perception.

Presence.summary: Force of personality and social influence.

Knowledge.summary: Memory, deduction, scholarship, and learned understanding.

experience_guidance.activation_cost: Spend 1 Hope for each relevant Experience used.
experience_guidance.stacking: Multiple relevant Experiences can be used on one action or reaction roll by spending Hope for each.

Bard.practical_role_summary: Social leader and flexible support character who bolsters allies through performance, words, and versatile magic.
Bard.beginner_tip: Use Rally and Hope proactively; your value is often measured by how much you improve the whole group.

Druid.practical_role_summary: Nature-focused spellcaster with transformation, elemental, healing, and battlefield-control options.
Druid.beginner_tip: Choose a clear identity between beast transformation, elemental expression, and restorative magic, then keep a few flexible cards.

Guardian.practical_role_summary: Durable frontline protector who controls threats, absorbs pressure, and punishes enemies for ignoring them.
Guardian.beginner_tip: Low Evasion is not failure; armor, thresholds, HP, and protective abilities are your intended defenses.

Ranger.practical_role_summary: Mobile hunter and wilderness expert who focuses prey, tracks danger, and may fight beside an animal companion.
Ranger.beginner_tip: Use positioning and Focus to keep pressure on a priority target instead of spreading attacks randomly.

Rogue.practical_role_summary: Stealth, infiltration, manipulation, mobility, and opportunistic damage.
Rogue.beginner_tip: Create advantages through darkness, deception, contacts, and positioning before relying on a direct attack.

Seraph.practical_role_summary: Divine champion who combines support, healing, protection, mobility, and frontline presence.
Seraph.beginner_tip: Balance restoration with decisive action; preventing harm can be more efficient than healing it later.

Sorcerer.practical_role_summary: Innate magical powerhouse with flexible elemental or primal expression and strong burst potential.
Sorcerer.beginner_tip: Stress is a spendable resource, but keep enough unmarked slots to avoid becoming Vulnerable at a bad moment.

Warrior.practical_role_summary: Weapon specialist with strong accuracy, damage, tactical control, and martial reliability.
Warrior.beginner_tip: Your weapon trait, range, and secondary weapon choice strongly shape your turn-to-turn options.

Wizard.practical_role_summary: Studied spellcaster with broad utility, knowledge, protective magic, and adaptable spell selection.
Wizard.beginner_tip: Use the loadout and vault deliberately; planning which cards are active is a core part of wizard play.

Arcana.theme: Innate, instinctive, elemental, and reality-shaping magic.

Blade.theme: Weapon mastery, martial force, and lethal technique.

Bone.theme: Tactics, movement, bodily mastery, and reading combat.

Codex.theme: Studied magic, written lore, grimoires, and flexible spellcraft.

Grace.theme: Charisma, performance, language, influence, and perception-shaping.

Midnight.theme: Shadows, secrecy, deception, hidden knowledge, and obscurity.

Sage.theme: Nature, creatures, growth, vitality, and wilderness magic.

Splendor.theme: Life, healing, radiant power, and limited influence over death.

Valor.theme: Protection, defense, courage, and shielding allies.

domain_card_management.starting_cards: Two Level 1 cards from the class's domains.
domain_card_management.acquisition: Gain one card at or below the PC's level from an accessible domain at every level-up, in addition to any card acquired through an advancement.
domain_card_management.vault: Acquired cards beyond the active loadout are inactive in the vault.
domain_card_management.rest_swap: At the start of a rest, before downtime moves, freely rearrange loadout and vault while keeping no more than five domain cards active.
domain_card_management.mid_scene_recall: Outside a rest, move a vaulted card into the loadout by marking Stress equal to that card's Recall Cost, and move an active card to the vault if needed to make space.
domain_card_management.new_card_exception: A newly acquired card may be placed into the loadout for free at level-up, moving another card to the vault if necessary.
domain_card_management.usage_limits: Track once-per-rest, once-per-long-rest, or other limits with tokens, card rotation, digital marks, or another clear method.

steps.name: Set the scene
steps.details: The GM describes the location, immediate situation, visible dangers, NPCs, and information the characters would readily notice.

steps.name: Ask and answer
steps.details: Players ask clarifying questions. The GM answers what the characters can know and may ask players questions that add useful details.

steps.name: Build on the fiction
steps.details: Players describe actions. Trivial actions or actions whose failure would be uninteresting succeed without a roll. Risky, uncertain, consequential actions trigger mechanics.

steps.name: Resolve and update
steps.details: Apply the outcome, describe how the world changes, move the spotlight, and begin the loop again.

core_gameplay_loop.golden_rule: The group may adjust rules by consent to support its preferred style.
core_gameplay_loop.rulings_over_rules: When an edge case is not covered, choose a ruling that follows the fiction and communicate consequences before a character commits.

spotlight_and_action_economy.default: No fixed initiative, rounds, or standard action/move/bonus-action structure.
how_spotlight_moves: To the character the fiction naturally focuses on.
To someone who has not been featured recently.
To the GM or a character selected by a triggered mechanic.
Back to the players after the GM finishes a GM turn.
spotlight_and_action_economy.fairness_rule: Do not let the loudest player monopolize the spotlight. Intentionally invite quieter players and characters whose choices matter now.
spotlight_and_action_economy.repeat_actions: A PC may act again before everyone else has acted when the fiction supports it, but the table should share attention.

optional_spotlight_tracker.procedure: Each time a PC takes an action, remove a token. If a PC has no tokens, spotlight another PC with tokens. Refill everyone after all players have spent their tokens.
optional_spotlight_tracker.purpose: Provides visible structure without restoring the obsolete beta action tracker.

action_rolls.when_to_roll: Roll when success is uncertain, failure is interesting, and the move carries meaningful risk or pressure.
when_not_to_roll: The task is trivial for the character.
Nothing interesting would happen on failure.
The result is already established by the fiction.
The GM only wants to delay progress without adding a meaningful consequence.

dice_pool.base_total_formula: Hope d12 + Fear d12 + relevant trait + declared modifiers + applicable extra dice

procedure: Choose or confirm the relevant trait.
Set or identify the Difficulty and communicate stakes.
Before rolling, declare Experiences, advantage/disadvantage, and features that must be activated in advance.
Roll the Duality Dice and all extra dice.
Add the total and announce both the total and whether the higher Duality Die is Hope or Fear.
Resolve success or failure, generate Hope or Fear if applicable, make any triggered GM move, and change the fiction.

critical_success.trigger: The Hope and Fear dice show the same face, regardless of modifiers.
critical_success.additional_effect: Clear 1 Stress and receive an extra benefit, opportunity, or advantage appropriate to the action.

success_with_hope.trigger: Total meets or exceeds Difficulty and Hope Die is higher.

success_with_fear.trigger: Total meets or exceeds Difficulty and Fear Die is higher.
success_with_fear.important: The attempted action succeeds. The complication does not erase that success.

failure_with_hope.trigger: Total is below Difficulty and Hope Die is higher.
failure_with_hope.typical_consequence: A minor complication, cost, lost position, or new pressure.

failure_with_fear.trigger: Total is below Difficulty and Fear Die is higher.
failure_with_fear.typical_consequence: A major complication, immediate danger, loss, separation, or escalation.

action_rolls.failing_forward: Every roll changes the scene. A failed lockpick might open the door too late, break a tool, alert a guard, expose a different route, or reveal that the lock is not the true obstacle; it should not simply produce no change.

special_rolls.trait_roll: An action or reaction roll that explicitly uses one of the six traits.

spellcast_roll.definition: A trait roll using the Spellcast trait specified by a subclass.
spellcast_roll.only_when_required: Do not make a Spellcast Roll merely because an action is magical; make one when the feature says to.
spellcast_roll.attack_interaction: A damaging Spellcast Roll is also an attack roll.
spellcast_roll.duration: Use the feature's stated duration. The GM may spend Fear to end a temporary spell effect. An unspecified spell ends when the caster chooses or when the fiction naturally ends it.
spellcast_roll.concentration: There is no universal one-spell concentration limit; multiple ongoing spells can coexist unless their text says otherwise.

reaction_roll.definition: A roll made to avoid or withstand an imminent effect.
reaction_roll.resource_generation: Does not generate Hope or Fear.
reaction_roll.gm_move_trigger: Does not independently trigger another GM move.
reaction_roll.critical: A critical reaction does not grant Hope or clear Stress, but it ignores effects that would still apply on a normal success.

group_action_roll.leader: One PC makes the main action roll.
group_action_roll.helpers: Each other participating PC makes a reaction roll with an appropriate trait.
group_action_roll.modifier: +1 to the leader for each helper success and -1 for each helper failure.
group_action_roll.use_case: The whole group is attempting one coordinated task together.

tag_team_roll.cost: 3 Hope paid by the initiating PC.
tag_team_roll.frequency: Each PC may initiate one Tag Team Roll per session, though a PC can participate in more than one.
tag_team_roll.procedure: Two PCs describe a combined maneuver, both make action rolls, then choose one complete roll result to resolve both actions.
tag_team_roll.resource_result: With Hope, each involved PC gains Hope. With Fear, the GM gains one Fear per involved PC.
tag_team_roll.attack_damage: On a successful combined attack, roll both damage totals, add them together, and treat the sum as one damage source. If damage types differ, choose which type applies.

advantage_and_disadvantage.advantage: Add a d6 advantage die to the roll total.
advantage_and_disadvantage.disadvantage: Subtract a d6 disadvantage die from the roll total.
advantage_and_disadvantage.cancellation: Advantage and disadvantage dice cancel one-for-one before rolling; do not roll both kinds in the same personal dice pool.
advantage_and_disadvantage.multiple_sources: Follow the specific feature text. Multiple uncancelled sources may create multiple dice where allowed.
advantage_and_disadvantage.help_an_ally_exception: Each helper spends 1 Hope and rolls an advantage die, but the acting PC adds only the single highest Help die result.
advantage_and_disadvantage.gm_adversaries: For an adversary with advantage, the GM rolls two d20s and keeps the higher; with disadvantage, keeps the lower.

core_uses.help_an_ally: Spend 1 Hope, explain the help, and roll a d6 Help die.
core_uses.use_experience: Spend 1 Hope per relevant Experience to add its modifier.
core_uses.tag_team: Spend 3 Hope to initiate a Tag Team Roll.
core_uses.hope_features: Pay the amount stated by a class, subclass, domain, ancestry, community, item, or other feature.

hope.timing_note: When a Hope Feature is used on the same action that rolls with Hope, the newly gained Hope may be spent on that feature if its timing permits.

fear.campaign_start: GM begins with 1 Fear per PC.
sources: Abilities, environments, adversaries, and other rules.
core_uses: Interrupt the players, steal the spotlight, and make a GM move.
Add an adversary's relevant Experience modifier to its roll.
End a temporary spell effect when the spell rules allow.
fear.gm_advice: Spend Fear to communicate intensity and escalation; do not hoard it until the pool is full.

combat.start: Combat begins when the fiction becomes a physical conflict. It uses the same spotlight and action-roll loop as every other scene.

player_attack_roll.roll: Duality Dice + weapon or spell trait + modifiers.
player_attack_roll.difficulty: Target adversary's Difficulty unless a feature specifies otherwise.
player_attack_roll.on_success: Roll damage and apply any effects.
player_attack_roll.unarmed_trait: Strength or Finesse, chosen by the GM based on the described attack.

adversary_attack_roll.natural_20: Automatically succeeds and deals critical damage by adding the maximum possible total of the attack's damage dice to the normal damage roll.

adversary_spotlight_options: Move within Close range and make a standard attack.
Move within Close range and use an adversary action.
Sprint within Far or Very Far range.
Do another action demanded by the fiction.
combat.additional_adversaries: After spotlighting an adversary through a GM move, spend additional Fear to spotlight additional adversaries before returning the spotlight to the PCs.

damage_rolls.weapon_formula: [Proficiency] × weapon damage die + one copy of the listed flat modifier.
damage_rolls.example: With Proficiency 2 and a d8+2 weapon, roll 2d8+2, not 2d8+4.
damage_rolls.spellcast_damage: When an effect says to deal damage using your Spellcast trait, roll a number of the named damage dice equal to the value of your Spellcast trait. If that trait is +0 or lower, roll no damage dice unless the feature says otherwise.
damage_rolls.critical_player_attack: Roll normal damage and add the maximum possible total of all damage dice, excluding flat modifiers.
damage_rolls.multi_target: If one ability targets several adversaries, make one attack roll and one damage roll, then apply the results to each target separately.
damage_rolls.simultaneous_sources: Add simultaneous damage sources together before comparing the total with thresholds.

damage_types.physical: Usually mundane weapons and unarmed attacks.
damage_types.resistance: Halve incoming damage of the resisted type, rounding up, before other reductions and threshold comparison. Multiple resistances to the same type do not stack.
damage_types.immunity: Ignore incoming damage of that type.
damage_types.mixed_damage: Resistance or immunity only applies if the target has it against both types.
damage_types.direct_damage: Cannot be reduced by marking Armor Slots.

evasion.meaning: How difficult a PC is to hit or affect with a hostile roll.
evasion.player_targets: Rolls against a PC normally compare against Evasion.
evasion.adversary_targets: PC attacks normally compare against adversary Difficulty.

hit_points_and_thresholds.concept: Damage is not subtracted from a hit-point total. Damage is compared with Major and Severe thresholds to determine how many HP slots are marked.

resolution.condition: Damage is 0 or less after reductions.
Damage is at least Major but below Severe.

threshold_formula.major: Equipped armor's base Major threshold + PC level + permanent or temporary threshold modifiers.
threshold_formula.severe: Equipped armor's base Severe threshold + PC level + permanent or temporary threshold modifiers.

hit_points_and_thresholds.falling: When the last HP slot is marked, the PC falls and immediately chooses a death move.
hit_points_and_thresholds.optional_massive_damage: If one source deals at least twice the Severe threshold, mark 4 HP instead of 3.

armor.armor_score: The number of Armor Slots available, up to 12.
armor.use: After taking damage, mark 1 Armor Slot to reduce the damage severity by one step: Severe to Major, Major to Minor, or Minor to no HP.
armor.not_numeric_reduction: Standard armor does not subtract a fixed number from damage unless an armor feature explicitly says it does.
armor.direct_damage: Armor Slots cannot reduce direct damage.
armor.temporary_armor_score: A temporary increase provides the same number of temporary slots; those slots vanish when the increase ends.
armor.repair: Clear marked Armor Slots through downtime or features.

uses: Paying costs for abilities, card recall, weapon swaps under pressure, and other features.
Representing strain, complications, and GM moves.
stress.last_slot: When the last Stress slot is marked, the character becomes Vulnerable until at least 1 Stress is cleared.
stress.overflow: When a character must mark Stress but has no open Stress slots, mark 1 HP instead.
stress.cost_limit: A character with all Stress marked cannot voluntarily activate a move that requires marking Stress.

order_of_operations_for_incoming_damage: Determine the total from the single attack or source, combining simultaneous sources when required.
Apply numerical damage reductions or other feature-specific adjustments in their stated order.
Optionally mark an Armor Slot to reduce severity by one step, unless the damage is direct or the armor forbids it.

range_movement_and_maps.default_style: Abstract narrative ranges; theater of the mind or maps are both supported.

Melee.fictional_distance: Close enough to touch; a few feet.

Very Far.optional_grid: 13 or more squares while still on the battle map

Out of Range.fictional_distance: Beyond Very Far and normally untargetable.

movement_under_pressure: When making an action roll under pressure, a character may also move to a location within Close range as part of that action.
If not already making an action roll, or moving farther than Close range, make an Agility Roll when safe movement is uncertain.
An adversary normally moves within Close as part of its action or sprints within Far or Very Far as a separate action.
range_movement_and_maps.line_of_sight: Ranged attacks normally require line of sight.
range_movement_and_maps.cover: Partial obstruction gives the attack disadvantage. Total obstruction blocks line of sight.
range_movement_and_maps.area_effect_default: Unless stated otherwise, all targets of a group effect must fit within Very Close range of one origin point inside the effect's range.

Hidden.effect: Rolls against the Hidden creature have disadvantage.
Hidden.requirements: The creature is out of sight from all enemies and its location is not otherwise known.
ends_when: An adversary moves to a position where it can see the creature.
The creature moves into an enemy's line of sight.

Restrained.effect: The creature cannot move but may still act from its current position.

Vulnerable.effect: All rolls targeting the creature have advantage.

conditions.same_condition_stacking: The same condition does not stack unless a rule explicitly says it does.
conditions.temporary_conditions: A PC usually clears a temporary condition by succeeding on an appropriate move. An adversary can clear one by spending its spotlight to do so.
conditions.special_conditions: A special condition ends only when its stated requirement is met.

general.three_short_rests_rule: After three consecutive short rests, the next rest must be a long rest.
general.domain_cards: At the start of either rest, freely rearrange loadout and vault.

interruption.long_rest: Provides only short-rest benefits if interrupted.

moves.tend_to_wounds: Clear 1d4 + Tier HP from yourself or an ally.
moves.repair_armor: Clear 1d4 + Tier Armor Slots on your armor or an ally's armor.
moves.prepare: Describe preparation and gain 1 Hope; if preparing with one or more party members, each participant gains 2 Hope.

short_rest.refresh: Refresh features limited per rest and end effects lasting until the next rest.

long_rest.fictional_length: Several in-world hours of camp, relaxation, or sleep.

moves.tend_to_all_wounds: Clear all HP from yourself or an ally.
moves.repair_all_armor: Clear all Armor Slots on your armor or an ally's armor.
moves.prepare: Describe preparation and gain 1 Hope; if preparing with one or more party members, each participant gains 2 Hope.
moves.work_on_a_project: With GM approval, begin or advance a long-term project using a countdown or an action roll.

long_rest.refresh: Refresh features limited per rest or long rest and end effects lasting until the next rest or long rest.
long_rest.gm_consequence: GM gains 1d4 + number of PCs Fear, up to the Fear cap, and may advance one long-term countdown.

death.trigger: A PC marks their last Hit Point.

Blaze of Glory.choice: Accept death and take one final action.
Blaze of Glory.resolution: With GM approval, the final action automatically critically succeeds, then the character dies.

resolution: The PC becomes temporarily unconscious and cannot act or move.
The unconscious PC cannot be targeted by attacks.
They awaken when an ally clears at least 1 of their marked HP or when the party finishes a long rest.

After falling unconscious, roll the Hope Die. If the result is less than or equal to the PC's level, gain a Scar: permanently cross out one Hope slot and define its lasting narrative impact with the GM.
If the final Hope slot is crossed out, the character's journey ends.

Risk It All.choice: Roll the Duality Dice and place survival in fate's hands.
Risk It All.hope_higher: Stay on your feet and clear HP and/or Stress totaling the Hope Die result, divided however you choose.
Risk It All.matching_dice: Stay on your feet and clear all HP and Stress.

death.replacement_character: If a PC dies, create a new PC at the party's current level before the next session.

leveling_and_tiers.method: The whole party levels together when the GM declares a narrative milestone, usually about every three sessions.
every_level: Choose two advancement slots from the current tier or a lower tier, obeying any two-slot costs and available marks.
Increase Major and Severe damage thresholds by 1.
Acquire one new domain card at or below the new level from an accessible class domain and place it in loadout or vault.

level_5: Clear the marks that limit which character traits can be improved in the new tier.
level_8: Clear the marks that limit which character traits can be improved in the new tier.

advancement_options_summary: Increase two currently eligible traits by +1.
Take the next subclass card: specialization, then mastery.
Increase Proficiency; this costs both advancement choices for that level when selected.
Multiclass at Level 5 or higher; this costs both advancement choices and restricts the conflicting subclass-upgrade option as shown on the sheet.

gain: Choose one of its two domains for future multiclass card access.
Take one foundation card from one of its subclasses.
multiclassing.spellcast_traits: If foundation cards specify different Spellcast traits, choose which applicable trait to use for a Spellcast Roll.
multiclassing.multiclass_domain_card_limit: Cards from the chosen multiclass domain must be at or below half the PC's current level, rounded up.
multiclassing.warning: Use the multiclass module and sheet instructions because subclass and multiclass advancement marks interact.

active_weapons.limit: Up to one primary and one secondary weapon, with a total burden of no more than two hands.
active_weapons.swap: Swap active and inventory weapons freely during a rest or calm moment; otherwise mark 1 Stress.
active_weapons.throwing: An equipped weapon may be thrown within Very Close range using Finesse. On success, deal its normal damage; it is no longer equipped until retrieved and re-equipped.

armor.danger_rule: Armor cannot normally be equipped while in danger or under pressure.
armor.inventory_rule: Armor is not carried in the standard inventory weapon slots.
armor.recalculate: When armor changes, recalculate thresholds and Armor Score and continue tracking that armor's marked slots.

countdowns.purpose: Track time, pressure, projects, rituals, hazards, reinforcements, escape, discovery, or any event approaching a trigger.
countdowns.basic_rule: A countdown starts at a value, decreases as it advances, and triggers its effect at 0.
countdowns.standard: Advances by 1 whenever a player makes an action roll, unless its rule says otherwise.

dynamic.purpose: Track positive progress, negative consequences, or both according to action-roll outcomes.

advanced_forms: Loop countdowns that reset after triggering.
Long-term countdowns that advance after rests.

principles: Begin and end with the fiction.
Collaborate, especially when a player's answer can enrich the world.
Ask questions and build on the answers.
Make the world feel alive through motives and consequences.
Be a fan of the PCs while embracing honest danger.
Keep promises, admit mistakes, and earn the group's trust.
Cut past unimportant material and keep the story moving.
Help players understand and use their resources.
calling_for_rolls: Let the player choose the approach; do not prescribe a solution.
Decide whether a roll is necessary.
Choose the trait that best matches the described approach.
Set Difficulty from the whole situation, not from a desire to force a preferred outcome.
Tell the player the stakes and any unavoidable consequence before rolling.
Offer a no-roll bargain with a clear cost or complication when that is more interesting.

difficulty.other_roll_against_adversary: Adversary Difficulty plus a relevant adversary Experience when appropriate.
difficulty.use: Choose the benchmark that best matches the fictional feat and circumstances. The official SRD gives trait-specific examples rather than one universal label.

practical_interpretation.20: Hard even for a skilled character.
practical_interpretation.30: Legendary or nearly impossible without exceptional positioning.

when_to_make_a_move: A PC fails an action roll.
A PC does something with unavoidable consequences.
The players give a golden opportunity that demands a response.
The table looks to the GM to say what happens next.

soft_vs_hard_moves.soft: Signals danger, reveals information, creates an opening, or offers time to respond.
soft_vs_hard_moves.hard: Applies an immediate cost, damage, separation, capture, lost opportunity, or other consequence without an additional chance to prevent it.
soft_vs_hard_moves.guideline: Favor softer moves on Hope results and harder moves on Fear results, adjusted for the fiction and agreed tone.

example_moves: Ask a question and build on the answer.
Make an NPC follow their motive.
Dangle a PC's goal to provoke action.
Reveal an unwelcome truth or unexpected danger.
Use a PC's backstory against them.

outcome_guidance.Critical Success: Let the player describe success and add an extra opportunity or advantage.
outcome_guidance.Success with Hope: Honor the success and show a favorable or open-ended world response.
outcome_guidance.Success with Fear: Honor the success, gain Fear, and add a minor consequence, cost, or complication.
outcome_guidance.Failure with Hope: Describe why the goal is not achieved, grant Hope, and add a minor consequence or useful opening.
outcome_guidance.Failure with Fear: Describe the failure, gain Fear, and add a major consequence or escalation.

adversary_stat_block_reading: Tier and type indicate expected scale and battlefield role.
Motives & Tactics tell the GM how the adversary behaves.
Difficulty is the usual target for PC rolls against it.
Thresholds convert incoming damage into marked HP.
HP and Stress track endurance and feature costs.
ATK and attack entries give the d20 bonus, range, damage, and type.
Experiences can be added by spending Fear when relevant.
Features define passive, action, reaction, and Fear-powered rules.

adversary_rolls.other_action: 1d20 plus any listed modifier against a GM-set Difficulty.
adversary_rolls.advantage: Roll two d20s and keep the higher.
adversary_rolls.disadvantage: Roll two d20s and keep the lower.

prep_advice: Prepare situations, motives, threats, and questions rather than scripting a single solution.
Create several things that can change when Hope or Fear appears.
Know what adversaries want before deciding how they fight.
Use countdowns for pressure the players can see and affect.
Plan places for short rests, long rests, discoveries, and character connections to matter.
Keep exact rules for chosen adversaries and environments nearby.

action_roll.situation: A character tries to pick a guild vault lock before patrols return.
action_roll.resolution: The lock opens. The PC gains 1 Hope, effectively replacing the Hope spent on the Experience. The table describes what opportunity the clean success creates.

success_with_fear.situation: A PC leaps a collapsing bridge and meets the Difficulty, but the Fear Die is higher.
success_with_fear.resolution: The PC reaches the far side; that success is not revoked. The GM gains 1 Fear and adds a cost, such as lost gear, a separated ally, or the bridge collapsing behind them.

damage_threshold.result_without_armor: Mark 2 HP because 10 meets Major but is below Severe.
damage_threshold.result_with_one_armor_slot: Mark 1 Armor Slot to reduce Major damage to Minor, then mark 1 HP.

critical_attack.explanation: Add the maximum possible result of the two d8s; do not double the +1 modifier.

group_action.situation: Four PCs try to hold a gate.
group_action.leader_roll: One PC makes a Strength action roll.
group_action.helpers: Three allies make appropriate reaction rolls.
group_action.example_result: Two helper successes and one failure give the leader a net +1.

pc_choices: One PC Tends to Wounds twice.
One repairs armor and prepares with another PC.
The paired preparers each gain 2 Hope.
short_rest.gm_fear: GM rolls 1d4 and gains that much Fear, respecting the cap.

before_campaign: Confirm final Core Set rules, not beta 1.5.
Agree on concept, aim, tone, and safety.
Choose a campaign frame or shared setting premise.
GM starts with 1 Fear per PC.
Each PC starts with 2 Hope, 6 Stress, class HP/Evasion, Proficiency 1, and starting gear.
before_action_roll: What is the PC trying to achieve?
What happens on failure or as an unavoidable cost?
Are Experiences, advantage, disadvantage, or pre-roll features being declared?
resolve_action_roll: Check matching Duality Dice first for a critical success.
Identify whether Hope or Fear is higher.
Apply success, failure, cost, complication, or GM move.
Update the fiction and move the spotlight.
player_attack: Choose target in range and confirm line of sight.
Roll Duality Dice with the weapon or spell trait against Difficulty.
On matching Duality Dice, add maximum damage dice to normal damage.
Target applies resistance, effects, thresholds, and optional armor.
Apply attack feature effects and narrate the result.
incoming_damage: Total simultaneous damage from one source.
Compare with Major and Severe thresholds.
Decide whether to mark one Armor Slot.
Mark 0-3 HP, or 4 with the optional massive-damage rule.
If last HP is marked, choose a death move.
end_of_short_rest: Each PC chooses two short-rest moves.
end_of_long_rest: Each PC chooses two long-rest moves.
GM gains 1d4 + number of PCs Fear.
GM may advance one long-term countdown.
level_up: Apply tier achievement if entering Level 2, 5, or 8.
Take one domain card at or below the new level.
Recalculate Evasion, HP, Stress, Proficiency, thresholds, and card loadout.
Update subclass or multiclass module if selected.

common_mistakes.correction: Use the finalized Core Set and September 2025 corrected SRD. The beta action tracker and older Hope/Fear, armor, and threshold rules are outdated.

common_mistakes.mistake: Running strict initiative rounds by habit.
common_mistakes.correction: Use the spotlight by default. The optional tracker is only a fairness aid.
Only roll when uncertainty and consequences are interesting.
Hope/Fear and success/failure are separate axes. Success with Fear still succeeds.
Compare damage with thresholds, then mark 1, 2, or 3 HP.
Normally mark one Armor Slot to reduce severity by one threshold.
When required to mark Stress with no slots open, mark 1 HP instead.

common_mistakes.mistake: Letting a full-Stress PC pay another Stress cost.
common_mistakes.correction: A PC cannot activate a move requiring Stress when all Stress is marked.
Only the five-card loadout is active; ancestry, community, and subclass cards are separate and always active.
Experiences should be specific enough that using one is a meaningful narrative choice.
Both currencies are intended to circulate and shape scenes.

common_mistakes.mistake: Negating a successful action with a complication.
common_mistakes.correction: On Success with Fear, preserve the achieved goal and attach a real but separate cost.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating range bands as exact measurements by default.
common_mistakes.correction: Ranges are fictional positioning categories; use the optional grid only when the table wants precision.
Rests recover resources but also generate GM Fear, and long rests can advance a long-term countdown.

pseudocode: if massive_damage_optional and final_damage >= 2 * severe_threshold: severity = 4
if armor_slot_used and not direct_damage: severity = max(0, severity - 1)
damage_to_hp.note: The optional massive-damage result is a special 4 HP result; table rulings should follow the official text if another effect also changes severity.

glossary.Action Roll: A Duality Dice roll made when a PC attempts a risky or uncertain move.
glossary.Armor Score: The maximum number of Armor Slots supplied by active armor and modifiers.
glossary.Armor Slot: A markable resource normally spent one at a time to reduce damage severity.
glossary.Critical Success: Matching Hope and Fear dice; automatic success with added benefit.
glossary.Difficulty: The target number an action roll must meet or exceed.
glossary.Domain: A themed ability deck. Each class has access to two.
glossary.Duality Dice: The paired Hope d12 and Fear d12 rolled by players.
glossary.Evasion: The usual target number for hostile rolls against a PC.
glossary.Experience: A character-specific phrase whose modifier can be added to a relevant roll by spending Hope.
glossary.Fear: GM metacurrency generated by Fear results, rests, and features.
glossary.GM Move: A narrative or mechanical action the GM makes when triggered by the fiction or dice.
glossary.Hope: PC metacurrency spent on Experiences, help, Tag Team Rolls, and features.
glossary.Loadout: Up to five acquired domain cards currently active.
glossary.Major Threshold: Damage at or above this number marks at least 2 HP.
glossary.Move: Anything a character or GM does that advances the fiction; only some moves require rolls.
glossary.Proficiency: Determines how many weapon damage dice a PC rolls.
glossary.Reaction Roll: A defensive or responsive roll that does not generate Hope/Fear or a new GM move.
glossary.Recall Cost: Stress required to swap a vaulted domain card into the loadout outside a rest.
glossary.Severe Threshold: Damage at or above this number marks 3 HP.
glossary.Spotlight: The table's current focus and the game's flexible turn structure.
glossary.Stress: A markable resource representing strain and powering many features.
glossary.Vault: Acquired domain cards not currently active.
glossary.Vulnerable: A condition that grants advantage to all rolls targeting the creature.

agenda.activity: Review concept, tone, safety, and the difference between Hope/Fear and success/failure.
Choose pregenerated PCs or finish Level 1 characters and connections.
Run a social or exploration scene with one low-stakes action roll, one Experience use, and Help an Ally.
Run a conflict that demonstrates spotlight movement, an adversary attack, damage thresholds, Armor Slots, and a condition.
Take a short rest and demonstrate downtime and GM Fear gain.
Resolve a final obstacle with a countdown or Tag Team Roll.
Debrief what was fun or confusing and record any agreed table rulings.

bard.name: Bard
bard.practical_role_summary: Social leader and flexible support character who bolsters allies through performance, words, and versatile magic.
bard.beginner_tip: Use Rally and Hope proactively; your value is often measured by how much you improve the whole group.

hope_feature.name: Make a Scene
hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope to temporarily Distract a target within Close range, giving them a -2 penalty to their Difficulty.

class_feature.name: Rally
class_feature.rules_text: Once per session, describe how you rally the party and give yourself and each of your allies a Rally Die. At level 1, your Rally Die is a d6. A PC can spend their Rally Die to roll it, adding the result to their action roll, reaction roll, damage roll, or to clear a number of Stress equal to the result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Rally Dice. At level 5, your Rally Die increases to a d8.

bard.srd_reference_text:
Bards are the most charismatic people in all the realms.
Members of this class are masters of captivation and
specialize in a variety of performance types, including singing,
playing musical instruments, weaving tales, or telling jokes.
Whether performing for an audience or speaking to an
individual, bards thrive in social situations. Members of this
profession bond and train at schools or guilds, but a current
of egotism runs through those of the bardic persuasion. While
they may be the most likely class to bring people together, a
bard of ill temper can just as easily tear a party apart.
DOMAINS - Grace & Codex
STARTING EVASION - 10
STARTING HIT POINTS - 5
CLASS ITEMS - A romance novel or a letter never opened
BARD’S HOPE FEATURE
Make a Scene: Spend 3 Hope to temporarily Distract a
target within Close range, giving them a -2 penalty to their
Difficulty.
CLASS FEATURE
Rally: Once per session, describe how you rally the party
and give yourself and each of your allies a Rally Die. At level
1, your Rally Die is a d6. A PC can spend their Rally Die to
roll it, adding the result to their action roll, reaction roll,
damage roll, or to clear a number of Stress equal to the
result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Rally
Dice. At level 5, your Rally Die increases to a d8.
BARD SUBCLASSES
Choose either the Troubadour or Wordsmith subclass.
TROUBADOUR
Play the Troubadour if you want to play music to bolster your
allies.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Presence
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Gifted Performer: You can play three different types of
songs, once each per long rest; describe how you perform
for others to gain the listed benefit:
• Relaxing Song: You and all allies within Close range clear
a Hit Point.
• Epic Song: Make a target within Close range temporarily
Vulnerable.
• Heartbreaking Song: You and all allies within Close
range gain a Hope.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Maestro. Your rallying songs steel the courage of those
who listen. When you give a Rally Die to an ally, they can
gain a Hope or clear a Stress.
MASTERY FEATURE
Virtuoso. You are among the greatest of your craft and your
skill is boundless. You can perform each of your “Gifted
Performer” feature’s songs twice per long rest.
WORDSMITH
Play the Wordsmith if you want to use clever wordplay and
captivate crowds.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Presence
FOUNDATION FEATURES
Rousing Speech: Once per long rest, you can give a
heartfelt, inspiring speech. All allies within Far range clear
2 Stress.
Heart of a Poet: After you make an action roll to impress,
persuade, or offend someone, you can spend a Hope to
add a d4 to the roll.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Eloquent. Your moving words boost morale. Once per
session, when you encourage an ally, you can do one of the B
following: t
w
• Allow them to find a mundane object or tool they need.
p
• Help an Ally without spending Hope. c
• Give them an additional downtime move during their D
next rest. b
T
MASTERY FEATURE
t
Epic Poetry. Your Rally Die increases to a d10. Additionally,
when you Help an Ally, you can narrate the moment as
if you were writing the tale of their heroism in a memoir. D
When you do, roll a d10 as your advantage die.
S
BACKGROUND QUESTIONS S
Answer any of the following background questions. You can C
also create your own questions. s
• Who from your community taught you to have such
confidence in yourself?
• You were in love once. Who did you adore, and how
did they hurt you?
• You’ve always looked up to another bard. Who are
they, and why do you idolize them?
CONNECTIONS
Ask your fellow players one of the following questions for
their character to answer, or create your own questions.
• What made you realize we were going to be such
good friends?
• What do I do that annoys you?
• Why do you grab my hand at night?
bard.source_note: Normalized SRD class section; includes subclass, background, connection, and class-module material appearing before the next class.

druid.name: Druid
druid.practical_role_summary: Nature-focused spellcaster with transformation, elemental, healing, and battlefield-control options.
druid.beginner_tip: Choose a clear identity between beast transformation, elemental expression, and restorative magic, then keep a few flexible cards.

hope_feature.name: Evolution
hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope to transform into a Beastform without marking a Stress. When you do, choose one trait to raise by +1 until you drop out of that Beastform.

druid.srd_reference_text:
Becoming a druid is more than an occupation; it’s a calling for
those who wish to learn from and protect the magic of the
wilderness. While one might underestimate a gentle druid who
practices the often-quiet work of cultivating flora, druids who
channel the untamed forces of nature are terrifying to behold.
Druids cultivate their abilities in small groups, often connected
by a specific ethos or locale, but some choose to work alone.
Through years of study and dedication, druids can learn to
transform into beasts and shape nature itself.
DOMAINS - Sage & Arcana
STARTING EVASION - 10
STARTING HIT POINTS - 6
CLASS ITEMS - A small bag of rocks and bones or a
strange pendant found in the dirt
DRUID’S HOPE FEATURE
Evolution: Spend 3 Hope to transform into a Beastform
without marking a Stress. When you do, choose one trait to
raise by +1 until you drop out of that Beastform.
CLASS FEATURES
Beastform: Mark a Stress to magically transform into a
creature of your tier or lower from the Beastform list. You
can drop out of this form at any time. While transformed,
you can’t use weapons or cast spells from domain cards,
but you can still use other features or abilities you have
access to. Spells you cast before you transform stay
active and last for their normal duration, and you can talk
and communicate as normal. Additionally, you gain the
Beastform’s features, add their Evasion bonus to your
Evasion, and use the trait specified in their statistics for
your attack. While you’re in a Beastform, your armor
becomes part of your body and you mark Armor Slots as
usual; when you drop out of a Beastform, those marked
Armor Slots remain marked. If you mark your last Hit Point,
you automatically drop out of this form.
Wildtouch: You can perform harmless, subtle effects that
involve nature—such as causing a flower to rapidly grow,
summoning a slight gust of wind, or starting a campfire—
at will.
DRUID SUBCLASSES
Choose either the Warden of the Elements or Warden of
Renewal subclass.
WARDEN OF THE ELEMENTS
Play the Warden of the Elements if you want to embody the
natural elements of the wild.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Instinct
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Elemental Incarnation: Mark a Stress to Channel one of the
following elements until you take Severe damage or until
your next rest:
• Fire: When an adversary within Melee range deals
damage to you, they take 1d10 magic damage.
• Earth: Gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to
your Proficiency.
• Water: When you deal damage to an adversary within
Melee range, all other adversaries within Very Close
range must mark a Stress.
• Air: You can hover, gaining advantage on Agility Rolls.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Elemental Aura: Once per rest while Channeling, you can
assume an aura matching your element. The aura affects
targets within Close range until your Channeling ends.
• Fire: When an adversary marks 1 or more Hit Points,
they must also mark a Stress.
• Earth: Your allies gain a +1 bonus to Strength.
• Water: When an adversary deals damage to you, you
can mark a Stress to move them anywhere within Very
Close range of where they are.
• Air: When you or an ally takes damage from an attack
beyond Melee range, reduce the damage by 1d8.
MASTERY FEATURE
Elemental Dominion: You further embody your element.
While Channeling, you gain the following benefit:
• Fire: You gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency for attacks
and spells that deal damage.
• Earth: When you would mark Hit Points, roll a d6 per Hit
Point marked. For each result of 6, reduce the number
of Hit Points you mark by 1.
• Water: When an attack against you succeeds, you
can mark a Stress to make the attacker temporarily
Vulnerable.
• Air: You gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion and can fly.
WARDEN OF RENEWAL
Play the Warden of Renewal if you want to use powerful magic
to heal your party.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Instinct
FOUNDATION FEATURES
Clarity of Nature: Once per long rest, you can create a
space of natural serenity within Close range. When you
spend a few minutes resting within the space, clear Stress
equal to your Instinct, distributed as you choose between
you and your allies.
e Regeneration: Touch a creature and spend 3 Hope. That
creature clears 1d4 Hit Points.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURES
Regenerative Reach: You can target creatures within Very

guardian.practical_role_summary: Durable frontline protector who controls threats, absorbs pressure, and punishes enemies for ignoring them.
guardian.beginner_tip: Low Evasion is not failure; armor, thresholds, HP, and protective abilities are your intended defenses.

hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope to clear 2 Armor Slots.

class_feature.name: Unstoppable
class_feature.rules_text: Once per long rest, you can become Unstoppable. You gain an Unstoppable Die. At level 1, your Unstoppable Die is a d4. Place it on your character sheet in the space provided, starting with the 1 value facing up. After you make a damage roll that deals 1 or more Hit Points to a target, increase the Unstoppable Die value by one. When the die’s value would exceed its maximum value or when the scene ends, remove the die and drop out of Unstoppable. At level 5, your Unstoppable Die increases to a d6. While Unstoppable, you gain the following benefits: • You reduce the severity of physical damage by one 8 threshold (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to None). • You add the current value of the Unstoppable Die to your damage roll. • You can’t be Restrained or Vulnerable. Tip: If your Unstoppable Die is a d4 and the 4 is currently facing up, you remove the die the next time you would increase it. However, if your Unstoppable Die has increased to a d6 and the 4 is currently facing up, you’ll turn it to 5 the next time you would increase it. In this case, you’ll remove the die after you would need to increase it higher than 6.

guardian.srd_reference_text:
The title of guardian represents an array of martial
professions, speaking more to their moral compass and
unshakeable fortitude than the means by which they fight.
While many guardians join groups of militants for either a
country or cause, they’re more likely to follow those few they
truly care for, majority be damned. Guardians are known for
fighting with remarkable ferocity even against overwhelming
odds, defending their cohort above all else. Woe betide those
who harm the ally of a guardian, as the guardian will answer
this injury in kind.
DOMAINS - Valor and Blade
STARTING EVASION - 9
STARTING HIT POINTS - 7
CLASS ITEMS - A totem from your mentor or a secret key

CLASS FEATURE
Unstoppable: Once per long rest, you can become
Unstoppable. You gain an Unstoppable Die. At level 1, your
Unstoppable Die is a d4. Place it on your character sheet
in the space provided, starting with the 1 value facing up.
After you make a damage roll that deals 1 or more Hit
Points to a target, increase the Unstoppable Die value by
one. When the die’s value would exceed its maximum value
or when the scene ends, remove the die and drop out of
Unstoppable. At level 5, your Unstoppable Die increases to
a d6.
While Unstoppable, you gain the following benefits:
• You reduce the severity of physical damage by one
8 threshold (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to
None).
• You add the current value of the Unstoppable Die to
your damage roll.
• You can’t be Restrained or Vulnerable.
Tip: If your Unstoppable Die is a d4 and the 4 is
currently facing up, you remove the die the next time
you would increase it. However, if your Unstoppable Die
has increased to a d6 and the 4 is currently facing up,
you’ll turn it to 5 the next time you would increase it. In
this case, you’ll remove the die after you would need to
increase it higher than 6.

ranger.name: Ranger
ranger.practical_role_summary: Mobile hunter and wilderness expert who focuses prey, tracks danger, and may fight beside an animal companion.
ranger.beginner_tip: Use positioning and Focus to keep pressure on a priority target instead of spreading attacks randomly.

hope_feature.name: Hold Them Off
hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope when you succeed on an attack with a weapon to use that same roll against two additional adversaries within range of the attack.

class_feature.name: Ranger’s Focus
class_feature.rules_text: Spend a Hope and make an attack against a target. On a success, deal your attack’s normal damage and temporarily make the attack’s target your Focus. Until this feature ends or you make a different creature your Focus, you gain the following benefits against your Focus: • You know precisely what direction they are in. • When you deal damage to them, they must mark a Stress. • When you fail an attack against them, you can end your Ranger’s Focus feature to reroll your Duality Dice.

ranger.srd_reference_text:
Rangers are highly skilled hunters who, despite their martial
abilities, rarely lend their skills to an army. Through mastery of
the body and a deep understanding of the wilderness, rangers
become sly tacticians, pursuing their quarry with cunning and
patience. Many rangers track and fight alongside an animal
companion with whom they’ve forged a powerful spiritual
bond. By honing their skills in the wild, rangers become expert
trackers, as likely to ensnare their foes in a trap as they are to
assail them head-on.
DOMAINS - Bone & Sage
STARTING EVASION - 12
STARTING HIT POINTS - 6
CLASS ITEMS - A trophy from your first kill or a seemingly
broken compass

additional adversaries within range of the attack.

a target. On a success, deal your attack’s normal damage
and temporarily make the attack’s target your Focus. Until
this feature ends or you make a different creature your
Focus, you gain the following benefits against your Focus:
• You know precisely what direction they are in.
• When you deal damage to them, they must mark a
Stress.
• When you fail an attack against them, you can end your
Ranger’s Focus feature to reroll your Duality Dice.

WORKING WITH
YOUR COMPANION
The following sections will run you through the basics of
working with your companion.
USING SPELLCAST ROLLS, HOPE, AND EXPERIENCES
Make a Spellcast Roll to connect with your companion and
command them to take action. Spend a Hope to add an
applicable Companion Experience to the roll. On a success
with Hope, if your next action builds on their success, you gain
advantage on the roll.
ATTACKING WITH YOUR COMPANION
When you command your companion to attack, they gain any
benefits that would normally only apply to you (such as the
effects of “Ranger’s Focus”). On a success, their damage roll
uses your Proficiency and their damage die.
TAKING DAMAGE AS STRESS
• When your companion would take any amount of damage,
they mark a Stress. When they mark their last Stress,
they drop out of the scene (by hiding, fleeing, or a similar
action). They remain unavailable until the start of your next
long rest, where they return with 1 Stress cleared.
• When you choose a downtime move that clears Stress
on yourself, your companion clears an equal number of
Stress.
LEVELING UP YOUR
COMPANION
When your character levels up, choose one available option
for your companion from the following list and mark it on your
sheet:
• Intelligent: Your companion gains a permanent +1 bonus
to a Companion Experience of your choice.
• Light in the Dark: Use this as an additional Hope slot your
character can mark.
• Creature Comfort: Once per rest, when you take time
during a quiet moment to give your companion love and
attention, you can gain a Hope or you can both clear a
Stress.
• Armored: When your companion takes damage, you can
mark one of your Armor Slots instead of marking one of
their Stress.
• Vicious: Increase your companion’s damage dice or range
by one step (d6 to d8, Close to Far, etc.).
• Resilient: Your companion gains an additional Stress slot.
• Bonded: When you mark your last Hit Point, your
companion rushes to your side to comfort you. Roll a
number of d6s equal to the unmarked Stress slots they
have and mark them. If any roll a 6, your companion helps
you up. Clear your last Hit Point and return to the scene.
• Aware: Your companion gains a permanent +2 bonus to
their Evasion.

rogue.name: Rogue
rogue.practical_role_summary: Stealth, infiltration, manipulation, mobility, and opportunistic damage.
rogue.beginner_tip: Create advantages through darkness, deception, contacts, and positioning before relying on a direct attack.

hope_feature.name: Rogue’s Dodge
hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope to gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion until the next time an attack succeeds against you. Otherwise, this bonus lasts until your next rest.

rogue.srd_reference_text:
Rogues are scoundrels, often in both attitude and practice.
Broadly known as liars and thieves, the best among this
class move through the world anonymously. Utilizing their
sharp wits and blades, rogues trick their foes through social
manipulation as easily as breaking locks, climbing through
windows, or dealing underhanded blows. These masters of
magical craft manipulate shadow and movement, adding an
array of useful and deadly tools to their repertoire. Rogues
frequently establish guilds to meet future accomplices, hire
out jobs, and hone secret skills, proving that there’s honor
among thieves for those who know where to look.
DOMAINS - Midnight & Grace
STARTING EVASION - 12
STARTING HIT POINTS - 6
CLASS ITEMS - A set of forgery tools or a grappling hook
ROGUE’S HOPE FEATURE
Rogue’s Dodge: Spend 3 Hope to gain a +2 bonus to your
Evasion until the next time an attack succeeds against you.
Otherwise, this bonus lasts until your next rest.
CLASS FEATURES
Cloaked: Any time you would be Hidden, you are instead
Cloaked. In addition to the benefits of the Hidden condition,
while Cloaked you remain unseen if you are stationary when
an adversary moves to where they would normally see you.
After you make an attack or end a move within line of sight
of an adversary, you are no longer Cloaked.
Sneak Attack: When you succeed on an attack while
Cloaked or while an ally is within Melee range of your target,
add a number of d6s equal to your tier to your damage roll.
• Level 1  Tier 1
• Levels 2–4  Tier 2
• Levels 5–7  Tier 3
• Levels 8–10  Tier 4
ROGUE SUBCLASSES
Choose either the Nightwalker or Syndicate subclass.
NIGHTWALKER
Play the Nightwalker if you want to manipulate shadows to
maneuver through the environment.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Finesse
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Shadow Stepper: You can move from shadow to shadow.
When you move into an area of darkness or a shadow cast
by another creature or object, you can mark a Stress to
disappear from where you are and reappear inside another
shadow within Far range. When you reappear, you are
Cloaked.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURES
Dark Cloud: Make a Spellcast Roll (15). On a success,
create a temporary dark cloud that covers any area within
Close range. Anyone in this cloud can’t see outside of it,
and anyone outside of it can’t see in. You’re considered
Cloaked from any adversary for whom the cloud blocks line
of sight.
Adrenaline: While you're Vulnerable, add your level to your
damage rolls.
MASTERY FEATURES
n
Fleeting Shadow: Gain a permanent +1 bonus to your
Evasion. You can use your “Shadow Stepper” feature to
move within Very Far range.
Vanishing Act: Mark a Stress to become Cloaked at any
, time. When Cloaked from this feature, you automatically
clear the Restrained condition if you have it. You remain
Cloaked in this way until you roll with Fear or until your next
rest.
SYNDICATE
Play the Syndicate if you want to have a web of contacts
everywhere you go.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Finesse
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Well-Connected: When you arrive in a prominent town or
environment, you know somebody who calls this place
home. Give them a name, note how you think they could be
useful, and choose one fact from the following list:
• They owe me a favor, but they’ll be hard to find.
S
• They’re going to ask for something in exchange. p
• They’re always in a great deal of trouble. t
T
• We used to be together. It’s a long story.
t
• We didn’t part on great terms.
p
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE S
t
Contacts Everywhere: Once per session, you can briefly call o
on a shady contact. Choose one of the following benefits a
and describe what brought them here to help you in this t
moment:
• They provide 1 handful of gold, a unique tool, or a
mundane object that the situation requires. D
• On your next action roll, their help provides a +3 bonus
S
to the result of your Hope or Fear Die.
• The next time you deal damage, they snipe from the S
shadows, adding 2d8 to your damage roll.
C
MASTERY FEATURE
Reliable Backup: You can use your “Contacts Everywhere”
feature three times per session. The following options are
added to the list of benefits you can choose from when you
use that feature:
• When you mark 1 or more Hit Points, they can rush out
to shield you, reducing the Hit Points marked by 1.
• When you make a Presence Roll in conversation, they
back you up. You can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.
BACKGROUND QUESTIONS
Answer any of the following background questions. You can
also create your own questions.
• What did you get caught doing that got you exiled
from your home community?
• You used to have a different life, but you’ve tried to
leave it behind. Who from your past is still chasing
you?
• Who from your past were you most sad to say
goodbye to?
CONNECTIONS
Ask your fellow players one of the following questions for
their character to answer, or create your own questions.
• What did I recently convince you to do that got us
both in trouble?
• What have I discovered about your past that I hold
secret from the others?
• Who do you know from my past, and how have they
influenced your feelings about me?

seraph.name: Seraph
seraph.practical_role_summary: Divine champion who combines support, healing, protection, mobility, and frontline presence.
seraph.beginner_tip: Balance restoration with decisive action; preventing harm can be more efficient than healing it later.

hope_feature.name: Life Support
hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope to clear a Hit Point on an ally within Close range.

class_feature.name: Prayer Dice
class_feature.rules_text: At the beginning of each session, roll a number of d4s equal to your subclass’s Spellcast trait and place them on your character sheet in the space provided. These are your Prayer Dice. You can spend any number of Prayer Dice to aid yourself or an ally within Far range. You can use a spent die’s value to reduce incoming damage, add to a roll’s result after the roll is made, or gain Hope equal to the result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Prayer Dice.

seraph.srd_reference_text:
Seraphs are divine fighters and healers imbued with sacred
purpose. A wide array of deities exist within the realms, and
thus numerous kinds of seraphs are appointed by these gods.
Their ethos traditionally aligns with the domain or goals of
their god, such as defending the weak, exacting vengeance,
protecting a land or artifact, or upholding a particular faith.
Some seraphs ally themselves with an army or locale, much
to the satisfaction of their rulers, but other crusaders fight in
opposition to the follies of the Mortal Realm. It is better to be
a seraph’s ally than their enemy, as they are terrifying foes to
those who defy their purpose.
DOMAINS - Splendor & Valor
STARTING EVASION - 9
STARTING HIT POINTS - 7
CLASS ITEMS - A bundle of offerings or a sigil of your god
SERAPH’S HOPE FEATURE
Life Support: Spend 3 Hope to clear a Hit Point on an ally
within Close range.
CLASS FEATURE
Prayer Dice: At the beginning of each session, roll a number
of d4s equal to your subclass’s Spellcast trait and place
them on your character sheet in the space provided. These
are your Prayer Dice. You can spend any number of Prayer
Dice to aid yourself or an ally within Far range. You can use
a spent die’s value to reduce incoming damage, add to a
roll’s result after the roll is made, or gain Hope equal to the
result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Prayer
Dice.
SERAPH SUBCLASSES
Choose either the Divine Wielder or Winged Sentinel subclass.
DIVINE WIELDER
Play the Divine Wielder if you want to dominate the battlefield
with a legendary weapon.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Strength
FOUNDATION FEATURES
Spirit Weapon: When you have an equipped weapon with
a range of Melee or Very Close, it can fly from your hand
to attack an adversary within Close range and then return
to you. You can mark a Stress to target an additional
adversary within range with the same attack roll.
Sparing Touch: Once per long rest, touch a creature and
clear 2 Hit Points or 2 Stress from them.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Devout: When you roll your Prayer Dice, you can roll an
additional die and discard the lowest result. Additionally,
you can use your “Sparing Touch” feature twice instead of
once per long rest.
MASTERY FEATURE
Sacred Resonance: When you roll damage for your “Spirit
Weapon” feature, if any of the die results match, double the
value of each matching die. For example, if you roll two 5s,
they count as two 10s.
WINGED SENTINEL
Play the Winged Sentinel if you want to take flight and strike
crushing blows from the sky.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Strength
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Wings of Light: You can fly. While flying, you can do the
following:
• Mark a Stress to pick up and carry another willing creature
approximately your size or smaller.
• Spend a Hope to deal an extra 1d8 damage on a
successful attack.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Ethereal Visage: Your supernatural visage strikes awe and fear.
While flying, you have advantage on Presence Rolls. When you
succeed with Hope on a Presence Roll, you can remove a Fear
from the GM’s Fear pool instead of gaining Hope.
MASTERY FEATURES
Ascendant: Gain a permanent +4 bonus to your Severe
damage threshold.
Power of the Gods: While flying, you deal an extra 1d12
damage instead of 1d8 from your “Wings of Light” feature.
BACKGROUND QUESTIONS
Answer any of the following background questions. You can
also create your own questions.
• Which god did you devote yourself to? What
incredible feat did they perform for you in a moment
of desperation?
• How did your appearance change after taking your
oath?
• In what strange or unique way do you communicate
with your god?
CONNECTIONS
Ask your fellow players one of the following questions for
their character to answer, or create your own questions.
• What promise did you make me agree to, should you
die on the battlefield?
• Why do you ask me so many questions about my
god?
e • You’ve told me to protect one member of our party
above all others, even yourself. Who are they and
why?
e
.

sorcerer.name: Sorcerer
sorcerer.practical_role_summary: Innate magical powerhouse with flexible elemental or primal expression and strong burst potential.
sorcerer.beginner_tip: Stress is a spendable resource, but keep enough unmarked slots to avoid becoming Vulnerable at a bad moment.

hope_feature.name: Volatile Magic
hope_feature.rules_text: Spend 3 Hope to reroll any number of your damage dice on an attack that deals magic damage.

sorcerer.srd_reference_text:
S
Not all innate magic users choose to hone their craft, but
C
those who do can become powerful sorcerers. The gifts of
these wielders are passed down through families, even if the
family is unaware of or reluctant to practice them. A sorcerer’s
abilities can range from the elemental to the illusionary and
beyond, and many practitioners band together into collectives P
based on their talents. The act of becoming a formidable t
sorcerer is not the practice of acquiring power, but learning
to cultivate and control the power one already possesses. The
magic of a misguided or undisciplined sorcerer is a dangerous
force indeed.
DOMAINS - Arcana & Midnight
STARTING EVASION - 10
STARTING HIT POINTS - 6
CLASS ITEMS - A whispering orb or a family heirloom
SORCERER’S HOPE FEATURE
Volatile Magic: Spend 3 Hope to reroll any number of your
damage dice on an attack that deals magic damage.
CLASS FEATURES
Arcane Sense: You can sense the presence of magical
people and objects within Close range.
Minor Illusion: Make a Spellcast Roll (10). On a success,
you create a minor visual illusion no larger than yourself
within Close range. This illusion is convincing to anyone at
Close range or farther.
Channel Raw Power: Once per long rest, you can place a
domain card from your loadout into your vault and choose
to either:
• Gain Hope equal to the level of the card.
• Enhance a spell that deals damage, gaining a bonus to
your damage roll equal to twice the level of the card.
P
y
SORCERER SUBCLASSES
Choose either the Elemental Origin or Primal Origin subclass.
ELEMENTAL ORIGIN
Play the Elemental Origin if you want to channel raw magic to
take the shape of a particular element.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Instinct
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Elementalist: Choose one of the following elements at
character creation: air, earth, fire, lightning, water.
You can shape this element into harmless effects.
Additionally, spend a Hope and describe how your control
over this element helps an action roll you’re about to make,
then either gain a +2 bonus to the roll or a +3 bonus to the
roll’s damage.
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Natural Evasion: You can call forth your element to protect
you from harm. When an attack roll against you succeeds,
you can mark a Stress and describe how you use your
element to defend you. When you do, roll a d6 and add its
result to your Evasion against the attack.
MASTERY FEATURE
Transcendence: Once per long rest, you can transform
into a physical manifestation of your element. When you
do, describe your transformation and choose two of the
following benefits to gain until your next rest:
• +4 bonus to your Severe threshold
• +1 bonus to a character trait of your choice
• +1 bonus to your Proficiency
• +2 bonus to your Evasion
PRIMAL ORIGIN
Play the Primal Origin if you want to extend the versatility of
your spells in powerful ways.
SPELLCAST TRAIT
Instinct
FOUNDATION FEATURE
Manipulate Magic: Your primal origin allows you to modify
the essence of magic itself. After you cast a spell or make
an attack using a weapon that deals magic damage, you
can mark a Stress to do one of the following:
• Extend the spell or attack’s reach by one range
• Gain a +2 bonus to the action roll’s result
• Double a damage die of your choice
• Hit an additional target within range
SPECIALIZATION FEATURE
Enchanted Aid: You can enhance the magic of others with
your essence. When you Help an Ally with a Spellcast Roll,
you can roll a d8 as your advantage die. Once per long rest,
after an ally has made a Spellcast Roll with your help, you
can swap the results of their Duality Dice.
MASTERY FEATURE
Arcane Charge: You can gather magical energy to enhance
your capabilities. When you take magic damage, you
become Charged. Alternatively, you can spend 2 Hope to
become Charged. When you successfully make an attack
that deals magic damage while Charged, you can clear your
Charge to either gain a +10 bonus to the damage roll or
gain a +3 bonus to the Difficulty of a reaction roll the spell
causes the target to make. You stop being Charged at your
next long rest.
BACKGROUND QUESTIONS
Answer any of the following background questions. You can
also create your own questions.
• What did you do that made the people in your
community wary of you?
• What mentor taught you to control your untamed
magic, and why are they no longer able to guide you?
• You have a deep fear you hide from everyone. What is
it, and why does it scare you?
CONNECTIONS
Ask your fellow players one of the following questions for
their character to answer, or create your own questions.
• Why do you trust me so deeply?
• What did I do that makes you cautious around me?
• Why do we keep our shared past a secret?
