(Elemental Spark), Verdant Defenders (Dryad, Oak Treant, Stag
Knight)
FEATURES
Chaos Magic Locus - Passive: When a PC makes a Spellcast Roll,
they must roll two Fear Dice and take the higher result.
What does it feel like to work magic in this chaos-touched place?
What do you fear will happen if you lose control of the spell?
The Indigo Flame - Passive: PCs who approach the central tree
can make a Knowledge Roll to try to identify the magic that
consumed this environment.
• On a success: They learn three of the below details. On a
success with Fear, they learn two.
• On a failure: They can mark a Stress to learn one and
gain advantage on the next action roll to investigate
this environment.
• Details: This is a result of Fallen magic. The corruption is
spread through the ashen moss. It can be cleansed only by a
ritual of nature magic with a Progress Countdown (8).
What Fallen cult corrupted these woods? What have they already
done with the cursed wood and sap from this tree?
Grasping Vines - Action: Animate vines bristling with thorns whip
out from the underbrush to ensnare the PCs. A target must
succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or become Restrained and
Vulnerable until they break free, clearing both conditions, with a
successful Finesse or Strength Roll or by dealing 10 damage to
the vines. When the target makes a roll to escape, they take
1d8+4 physical damage and lose a Hope.
What painful memories do the vines bring to the surface as they
pierce flesh?
Charcoal Constructs - Action: Warped animals wreathed in indigo
fl ame trample through a point of your choice. All targets within
Close range of that point must make an Agility Reaction Roll.
Targets who fail take 3d12+3 physical damage. Targets who
succeed take half damage instead.
Are these real animals consumed by the fl ame or merely constructs of
the corrupting magic?
Choking Ash - Reaction: Countdown (Loop ). When the PCs enter
the Burning Heart of the Woods, activate the countdown. When
it triggers, all characters must make a Strength or Instinct
Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 4d6+5 direct physical
damage. Targets who succeed take half damage. Protective
masks or clothes give advantage on the reaction roll.
What hallucinations does the ash induce? What incongruous taste
does it possess?

castle_siege.name: Castle Siege
castle_siege.description: An active siege with an attacking force fighting to gain entry to a fortifi ed castle.
castle_siege.impulses: Bleed out the will to fight, breach the walls, build tension
castle_siege.potential_adversaries: Mercenaries (Harrier, Sellsword, Spellblade, Weaponmaster), Noble Forces (Archer Squadron, Conscript, Elite Soldier, Knight of the Realm)
castle_siege.srd_reference_text:
An active siege with an attacking force fighting to gain entry to a
fortifi ed castle.
Impulses: Bleed out the will to fight, breach the walls, build
tension
Difficulty: 17
Potential Adversaries: Mercenaries (Harrier, Sellsword,
Spellblade, Weaponmaster), Noble Forces (Archer Squadron,
Conscript, Elite Soldier, Knight of the Realm)
FEATURES
Secret Entrance - Passive: A PC can find or recall a secret way into
the castle with a successful Instinct or Knowledge Roll.
How do they get in without revealing the pathway to the attackers?
Are any of the defenders monitoring this path?
Siege Weapons (Environment Change) - Action: Consequence
Countdown (6). The attacking force deploys siege weapons to
try to raze the defenders’ fortifi cations. Activate the countdown
when the siege begins (for a protracted siege, make this a
long-term countdown instead). When it triggers, the defenders’
fortifi cations have been breached and the attackers fl ood inside.
You gain 2 Fear, then shift to the Pitched Battle environment and
spotlight it.
What siege weapons are being deployed? Are they magical, mundane,
or a mixture of both? What defenses must the characters overcome to
storm the castle?
Reinforcements! - Action: Summon a Knight of the Realm, a
number of Tier 3 Minions equal to the number of PCs, and two
adversaries of your choice within Far range of a chosen PC as
reinforcements. The Knight of the Realm immediately takes the
spotlight.
Who are they targeting first? What formation do they take?
Collateral Damage - Reaction: When an adversary is defeated, you
can spend a Fear to have a stray attack from a siege weapon hit
a point on the battlefi eld. All targets within Very Close range of
that point must make an Agility Reaction Roll.
• Targets who fail take 3d8+3 physical or magic damage and
must mark a Stress.
• Targets who succeed must mark a Stress.
What debris is scattered by the attack? What is broken by the strike
that can’t be easily mended?

pitched_battle.name: Pitched Battle
pitched_battle.description: A massive combat between two large groups of armed combatants.
pitched_battle.impulses: Seize people, land, and wealth, spill blood for greed and glory
pitched_battle.potential_adversaries: Mercenaries (Sellsword, Harrier, Spellblade, Weaponmaster), Noble Forces (Archer Squadron, Conscript, Elite Soldier, Knight of the Realm)
feature_names: Adrift on a Sea of Steel
pitched_battle.srd_reference_text:
A massive combat between two large groups of armed combatants.
Impulses: Seize people, land, and wealth, spill blood for greed
and glory
Difficulty: 17
Potential Adversaries: Mercenaries (Sellsword, Harrier,
Spellblade, Weaponmaster), Noble Forces (Archer Squadron,
Conscript, Elite Soldier, Knight of the Realm)
FEATURES
Adrift on a Sea of Steel - Passive: Traversing a battlefi eld during an
active combat is extremely dangerous. A PC must succeed on
an Agility Roll to move at all, and can only go up to Close range
on a success. If an adversary is within Melee range of them, they
must mark a Stress to make an Agility Roll to move.
Do the combatants mistake you for the enemy or consider you
interlopers? Can you tell the diff erence between friend and foe in
the fray?
Raze and Pillage - Action: The attacking force raises the stakes by
lighting a fire, stealing a valuable asset, kidnapping an important
person, or killing the populace.
What is valuable here? Who is most vulnerable?
War Magic - Action: Spend a Fear as a mage from one side uses
large-scale destructive magic. Pick a point on the battlefi eld
within Very Far range of the mage. All targets within Close range
of that point must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail
take 3d12+8 magic damage and must mark a Stress.
What form does the attack take—fireball, raining acid, a storm of
blades? What tactical objective is this attack meant to accomplish,
and what comes next?
Reinforcements! - Action: Summon a Knight of the Realm, a
number of Tier 3 Minions equal to the number of PCs, and two
adversaries of your choice within Far range of a chosen PC
as reinforcements. The Knight of the Realm immediately
takes the spotlight.
Who are they targeting first? What formation do they take?

chaos_realm.name: Chaos Realm
chaos_realm.description: An otherworldly space where the laws of reality are unstable and dangerous.
chaos_realm.impulses: Annihilate certainty, consume power, defy logic
feature_names: Everything You Are This Place Will Take from You
chaos_realm.srd_reference_text:
An otherworldly space where the laws of reality are unstable and
dangerous.
Impulses: Annihilate certainty, consume power, defy logic
Difficulty: 20
Potential Adversaries: Outer Realms Monstrosities
(Abomination, Corruptor, Thrall)
FEATURES
Impossible Architecture - Passive: Up is down, down is right, right
is starward. Gravity and directionality themselves are in flux, and
any attempt to move through this realm is an odyssey unto itself,
requiring a Progress Countdown (8). On a failure, a PC must
mark a Stress in addition to the roll’s other consequences.
What does it feel like to move in a space so alien to the Mortal Realm?
What landmark or point do you fi xate on to maintain your balance?
What bizarre landmarks do you traverse on your journey?
Everything You Are This Place Will Take from You - Action:
Countdown (Loop 1d4). Activate the countdown. When it
triggers, all PCs must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or
their highest trait is temporarily reduced by 1d4 unless they
mark a number of Stress equal to its value. Any lost trait points
are regained if the PC critically succeeds or escapes the
Chaos Realm.
How does this place try to steal from you that which makes you
legendary? What does it feel like to have this power taken from you?
Unmaking - Action: Spend a Fear to force a PC to make a Strength
Reaction Roll. On a failure, they take 4d10 direct magic damage.
On a success, they must mark a Stress.
What glimpse of other worlds do you catch while this place tries to
unmake you? What core facet of your personality does the unmaking
try to erase?
Outer Realms Predators - Action: Spend a Fear to summon an
Outer Realms Abomination, an Outer Realms Corruptor, and 2d6
Outer Realms Thralls, who appear at Close range of a chosen
PC in defi ance of logic and causality. Immediately spotlight one
of these adversaries, and you can spend an additional Fear to
automatically succeed on that adversary’s standard attack.
What half-consumed remnants of the shattered world do these
monstrosities cast aside in pursuit of living flesh? What jagged
refl ections of former personhood do you catch between moments
of unquestioning malice?
Disorienting Reality - Reaction: On a result with Fear, you can ask
the PC to describe which of their fears the Chaos Realm evokes
as a vision of reality unmakes and reconstitutes itself to the PC.
The PC loses a Hope. If it is their last Hope, you gain a Fear.
What moment do they see? If it’s a memory, how is it warped by this
place? How hard will it be to hold on to the real memory?

divine_usurpation.name: Divine Usurpation
divine_usurpation.description: A massive ritual designed to breach the gates of the Hallows Above and unseat the New Gods themselves.
divine_usurpation.potential_adversaries: Arch-Necromancer, Fallen Shock Troops, Mortal Hunter, Oracle of Doom, Perfected Zombie
divine_usurpation.srd_reference_text:
A massive ritual designed to breach the gates of the Hallows Above
and unseat the New Gods themselves.
Impulses: Collect power, overawe, silence dissent
Difficulty: 20
Potential Adversaries: Arch-Necromancer, Fallen Shock
Troops, Mortal Hunter, Oracle of Doom, Perfected Zombie
FEATURES
Final Preparations - Passive: When the environment first takes
the spotlight, designate one adversary as the Usurper seeking to
overthrow the gods. Activate a Long-Term Countdown (8) as the
Usurper assembles what they need to conduct the ritual. When
it triggers, spotlight this environment to use the “Beginning of
the End” feature. While this environment remains in play, you
can hold up to 15 Fear.
What does the Usurper still require: The heart of a High Seraph? The
lodestone of an ancient waygate? The loyalty of two archenemies? The
heartbroken tears of a pure soul?
Divine Blessing - Passive: When a PC critically succeeds, they can
spend 2 Hope to refresh an ability normally limited by uses (such
as once per rest, once per session).
What god favors you as you fight against this usurpation? How does
your renewed power refl ect their infl uence?
Defi lers Abound - Action: Spend 2 Fear to summon 1d4+2 Fallen
Shock Troops that appear within Close range of the Usurper to
assist their divine siege. Immediately spotlight the Shock Troops
to use a “Group Attack” action.
Which High Fallen do these troops serve? Which god’s flesh do they
wish to feast upon?
Godslayer - Action: If the Divine Siege Countdown (see “Beginning
of the End”) has triggered, you can spend 3 Fear to describe the
Usurper slaying one of the gods of the Hallows Above, feasting
upon their power and growing stronger. The Usurper clears 2
HP. Increase their Difficulty, damage, attack modifi er, or give
them a new feature from the slain god.
Which god meets their end? What are their last words? How does the
Usurper’s new stolen power manifest?
Beginning of the End - Reaction: When the “Final Preparations”
long-term countdown triggers, the Usurper begins hammering
on the gates of the Hallows themselves. Activate a Divine Siege
Countdown (10). Spotlight the Usurper to describe the Usurper’s
assault and tick down this countdown by 1. If the Usurper
takes Major or greater damage, tick up the countdown by 1.
When it triggers, the Usurper shatters the barrier between the
Mortal Realm and the Hallows Above to slay the gods and take
their place. You gain a Fear for each unmarked HP the Usurper
has. You can immediately use the “Godslayer” feature without
spending Fear to make an additional GM move.
How does the Mortal Realm writhe as the natural order is violated?
What mortals witness this blasphemy from afar?
Ritual Nexus - Reaction: On any failure with Fear against the
Usurper, the PC must mark 1d4 Stress from the backlash of
magical power.
What visions of failures past torment you as your eff orts fall short?
How are these memories twisted by the Usurper?

imperial_court.name: Imperial Court
imperial_court.description: The majestic domain of a powerful empire, lavishly appointed with stolen treasures.
imperial_court.impulses: Justify and perpetuate imperial rule, seduce rivals with promises of power and comfort
imperial_court.potential_adversaries: Bladed Guard, Courtesan, Knight of the Realm, Monarch, Spy
imperial_court.srd_reference_text:
The majestic domain of a powerful empire, lavishly appointed with
stolen treasures.
Impulses: Justify and perpetuate imperial rule, seduce rivals with
promises of power and comfort
Difficulty: 20
Potential Adversaries: Bladed Guard, Courtesan, Knight of the
Realm, Monarch, Spy
FEATURES
All Roads Lead Here - Passive: While in the Imperial Court, a
PC has disadvantage on Presence Rolls made to take actions
that don’t fi t the imperial way of life or support the empire’s
dominance.
How does the way language is used make even discussing alternative
ways of living diffi cult? What obvious benefits for loyalty create
friction when you try to discuss alternatives?
Rival Vassals - Passive: The PCs can find imperial subjects,
vassals, and supplicants in the court, each vying for favor,
seeking proximity to power, exchanging favors for loyalty, and
elevating their status above others’. Some might be desperate
to undermine their rivals, while others might even be open to
discussions that verge on sedition.
How do they benefit from vassalage, and what has it cost them?
What exploitation drives them to consider opposing the unstoppable?
The Gravity of Empire - Action: Spend a Fear to present a PC with
a golden opportunity or offer to satisfy a major goal in exchange
for obeying or supporting the empire. The target must make a
Presence Reaction Roll. On a failure, they must mark all their
Stress or accept the offer. If they have already marked all their
Stress, they must accept the offer or exile themselves from the
empire. On a success, they must mark 1d4 Stress as they’re
taxed by temptation.
What do the PCs want so desperately they might consider throwing
in with this ruthless power? How did imperial agents learn the PC’s
greatest desires?
Imperial Decree - Action: Spend a Fear to tick down a long-term
countdown related to the empire’s agenda by 1d4. If this
triggers the countdown, a proclamation related to the agenda
is announced at court as the plan is executed.
What display of power or transfer of wealth was needed to expedite
this plan? Whose lives were disrupted or upended to make this
happen?
Eyes Everywhere - Reaction: On a result with Fear, you can spend
a Fear to have someone loyal to the empire overhear seditious
talk within the court. A PC must succeed on an Instinct Reaction
Roll to notice that the group has been overheard so they can try
to intercept the witness before the PCs are exposed.
How has the empire compromised this witness? Why is their first
impulse to protect the empire, even if doesn’t treat them well?

necromancer_s_ossuary.name: Necromancer’S Ossuary
necromancer_s_ossuary.description: A dusty crypt with a library, twisting corridors, and abundant sarcophagi, spattered with the blood of ill-fated invaders.
necromancer_s_ossuary.impulses: Confound intruders, delve into secrets best left buried, manifest unlife, unleash a tide of undead
necromancer_s_ossuary.srd_reference_text:
A dusty crypt with a library, twisting corridors, and abundant
sarcophagi, spattered with the blood of ill-fated invaders.
Impulses: Confound intruders, delve into secrets best left buried,
manifest unlife, unleash a tide of undead
Difficulty: 19
Potential Adversaries: Arch-Necromancer’s Host (Perfected
Zombie, Zombie Legion)
FEATURES
No Place for the Living - Passive: A feature or action that clears HP
requires spending a Hope to use. If it already costs Hope, a PC
must spend an additional Hope.
What does it feel like to try to heal in a place so antithetical to life?
Centuries of Knowledge - Passive: A PC can investigate the library
and laboratory and make a Knowledge Roll to learn information
related to arcana, local history, and the Necromancer’s plans.
What are the names of the tomes? What project is the necromancer
working on and what does it communicate about their plans?
Skeletal Burst - Action: All targets within Close range of a point
you choose in this environment must succeed on an Agility
Reaction Roll or take 4d8+8 physical damage from skeletal
shrapnel as part of the ossuary detonates around them.
What ancient skeletal architecture is destroyed? What bones stick in
your armor?
Aura of Death - Action: Once per scene, roll a d4. Each undead
within Far range of the Necromancer can clear HP and Stress
equal to the result rolled. The undead can choose how that
number is divided between HP and Stress.
How does their renewed vigor manifest? Do they look more lifelike or,
paradoxically, are they more decayed but vigorous?
They Just Keep Coming! - Action: Spend a Fear to summon 1d6
Rotted Zombies, two Perfected Zombies, or a Zombie Legion,
who appear at Close range of a chosen PC.
Who were these people before they became the necromancer’s pawns?
What vestiges of those lives remain for the heroes to see?

battle_points.purpose: Estimate an encounter's opposition budget, then adjust for terrain, objectives, player experience, and desired danger.
workflow: Choose the encounter tier from party level.
Choose a desired intensity and starting battle-point budget from the official GM guidance.
Select adversaries whose tier and role support the scene's objective.
Spend points according to adversary role and tier guidance in the current SRD.
Add an environment when the location should act mechanically.
Review action economy, spotlight frequency, Relentless features, minion/horde rules, and escape routes.
During play, adjust through Fear, reinforcements, objectives, and fiction rather than secretly rewriting successful player outcomes.
battle_points.important_limit: Use the exact current SRD battle-point table when numeric construction precision is required; this database emphasizes the procedure and full adversary catalog.

adversary_stat_reading: Tier and type indicate expected scale and battlefield role.
Motives & Tactics tell the GM how the adversary behaves.
Difficulty is the usual target for PC rolls against it.
Thresholds convert incoming damage into marked HP.
HP and Stress track endurance and feature costs.
ATK and attack entries give the d20 bonus, range, damage, and type.
Experiences can be added by spending Fear when relevant.
Features define passive, action, reaction, and Fear-powered rules.
gm_move_triggers: A PC fails an action roll.
A PC does something with unavoidable consequences.
The players give a golden opportunity that demands a response.
The table looks to the GM to say what happens next.

countdowns.purpose: Track time, pressure, projects, rituals, hazards, reinforcements, escape, discovery, or any event approaching a trigger.
countdowns.basic_rule: A countdown starts at a value, decreases as it advances, and triggers its effect at 0.
countdowns.standard: Advances by 1 whenever a player makes an action roll, unless its rule says otherwise.

dynamic.purpose: Track positive progress, negative consequences, or both according to action-roll outcomes.

advanced_forms: Loop countdowns that reset after triggering.
Long-term countdowns that advance after rests.

action_roll.situation: A character tries to pick a guild vault lock before patrols return.
action_roll.resolution: The lock opens. The PC gains 1 Hope, effectively replacing the Hope spent on the Experience. The table describes what opportunity the clean success creates.

success_with_fear.situation: A PC leaps a collapsing bridge and meets the Difficulty, but the Fear Die is higher.
success_with_fear.resolution: The PC reaches the far side; that success is not revoked. The GM gains 1 Fear and adds a cost, such as lost gear, a separated ally, or the bridge collapsing behind them.

damage_threshold.result_without_armor: Mark 2 HP because 10 meets Major but is below Severe.
damage_threshold.result_with_one_armor_slot: Mark 1 Armor Slot to reduce Major damage to Minor, then mark 1 HP.

critical_attack.explanation: Add the maximum possible result of the two d8s; do not double the +1 modifier.

group_action.situation: Four PCs try to hold a gate.
group_action.leader_roll: One PC makes a Strength action roll.
group_action.helpers: Three allies make appropriate reaction rolls.
group_action.example_result: Two helper successes and one failure give the leader a net +1.

pc_choices: One PC Tends to Wounds twice.
One repairs armor and prepares with another PC.
The paired preparers each gain 2 Hope.
short_rest.gm_fear: GM rolls 1d4 and gains that much Fear, respecting the cap.

agenda.activity: Review concept, tone, safety, and the difference between Hope/Fear and success/failure.
Choose pregenerated PCs or finish Level 1 characters and connections.
Run a social or exploration scene with one low-stakes action roll, one Experience use, and Help an Ally.
Run a conflict that demonstrates spotlight movement, an adversary attack, damage thresholds, Armor Slots, and a condition.
Take a short rest and demonstrate downtime and GM Fear gain.
Resolve a final obstacle with a countdown or Tag Team Roll.
Debrief what was fun or confusing and record any agreed table rulings.

teaching_order: Duality Dice and the five outcomes.

before_campaign: Confirm final Core Set rules, not beta 1.5.
Agree on concept, aim, tone, and safety.
Choose a campaign frame or shared setting premise.
GM starts with 1 Fear per PC.
Each PC starts with 2 Hope, 6 Stress, class HP/Evasion, Proficiency 1, and starting gear.
before_action_roll: What is the PC trying to achieve?
What happens on failure or as an unavoidable cost?
Are Experiences, advantage, disadvantage, or pre-roll features being declared?
resolve_action_roll: Check matching Duality Dice first for a critical success.
Identify whether Hope or Fear is higher.
Apply success, failure, cost, complication, or GM move.
Update the fiction and move the spotlight.
player_attack: Choose target in range and confirm line of sight.
Roll Duality Dice with the weapon or spell trait against Difficulty.
On matching Duality Dice, add maximum damage dice to normal damage.
Target applies resistance, effects, thresholds, and optional armor.
Apply attack feature effects and narrate the result.
incoming_damage: Total simultaneous damage from one source.
Compare with Major and Severe thresholds.
Decide whether to mark one Armor Slot.
Mark 0-3 HP, or 4 with the optional massive-damage rule.
If last HP is marked, choose a death move.
end_of_short_rest: Each PC chooses two short-rest moves.
end_of_long_rest: Each PC chooses two long-rest moves.
GM gains 1d4 + number of PCs Fear.
GM may advance one long-term countdown.
level_up: Apply tier achievement if entering Level 2, 5, or 8.
Take one domain card at or below the new level.
Recalculate Evasion, HP, Stress, Proficiency, thresholds, and card loadout.
Update subclass or multiclass module if selected.

common_mistakes.correction: Use the finalized Core Set and September 2025 corrected SRD. The beta action tracker and older Hope/Fear, armor, and threshold rules are outdated.

common_mistakes.mistake: Running strict initiative rounds by habit.
common_mistakes.correction: Use the spotlight by default. The optional tracker is only a fairness aid.
Only roll when uncertainty and consequences are interesting.
Hope/Fear and success/failure are separate axes. Success with Fear still succeeds.
Compare damage with thresholds, then mark 1, 2, or 3 HP.
Normally mark one Armor Slot to reduce severity by one threshold.
When required to mark Stress with no slots open, mark 1 HP instead.

common_mistakes.mistake: Letting a full-Stress PC pay another Stress cost.
common_mistakes.correction: A PC cannot activate a move requiring Stress when all Stress is marked.
Only the five-card loadout is active; ancestry, community, and subclass cards are separate and always active.
Experiences should be specific enough that using one is a meaningful narrative choice.
Both currencies are intended to circulate and shape scenes.

common_mistakes.mistake: Negating a successful action with a complication.
common_mistakes.correction: On Success with Fear, preserve the achieved goal and attach a real but separate cost.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating range bands as exact measurements by default.
common_mistakes.correction: Ranges are fictional positioning categories; use the optional grid only when the table wants precision.
Rests recover resources but also generate GM Fear, and long rests can advance a long-term countdown.

glossary.Action Roll: A Duality Dice roll made when a PC attempts a risky or uncertain move.
glossary.Armor Score: The maximum number of Armor Slots supplied by active armor and modifiers.
glossary.Armor Slot: A markable resource normally spent one at a time to reduce damage severity.
glossary.Critical Success: Matching Hope and Fear dice; automatic success with added benefit.
glossary.Difficulty: The target number an action roll must meet or exceed.
glossary.Domain: A themed ability deck. Each class has access to two.
glossary.Duality Dice: The paired Hope d12 and Fear d12 rolled by players.
glossary.Evasion: The usual target number for hostile rolls against a PC.
glossary.Experience: A character-specific phrase whose modifier can be added to a relevant roll by spending Hope.
glossary.Fear: GM metacurrency generated by Fear results, rests, and features.
glossary.GM Move: A narrative or mechanical action the GM makes when triggered by the fiction or dice.
glossary.Hope: PC metacurrency spent on Experiences, help, Tag Team Rolls, and features.
glossary.Loadout: Up to five acquired domain cards currently active.
glossary.Major Threshold: Damage at or above this number marks at least 2 HP.
glossary.Move: Anything a character or GM does that advances the fiction; only some moves require rolls.
glossary.Proficiency: Determines how many weapon damage dice a PC rolls.
glossary.Reaction Roll: A defensive or responsive roll that does not generate Hope/Fear or a new GM move.
glossary.Recall Cost: Stress required to swap a vaulted domain card into the loadout outside a rest.
glossary.Severe Threshold: Damage at or above this number marks 3 HP.
glossary.Spotlight: The table's current focus and the game's flexible turn structure.
glossary.Stress: A markable resource representing strain and powering many features.
glossary.Vault: Acquired domain cards not currently active.
glossary.Vulnerable: A condition that grants advantage to all rolls targeting the creature.

session_zero.goal: Agree on the kind of game everyone is consenting to play before long-term play begins.
recommended_topics: Concept: What is the campaign about?
Aim: What are the characters expected to pursue and what kind of play should be emphasized?
Tone: Heroic, tragic, cozy, horror-leaning, comedic, political, romantic, or another agreed mixture.
Safety: Lines, veils, an X-card or equivalent pause/edit tool, and an open-door policy.
Campaign frame or setting assumptions.
Character creation boundaries and allowed options.
How much player-authored worldbuilding everyone enjoys.
Expected session length, attendance, scheduling, and communication.
PvP, secrets, romance, character death, and intra-party conflict.
Accessibility needs and any adjustments to cards, dice, visual trackers, audio, or pacing.

safety_tools.lines: Content that does not appear in the game.
safety_tools.veils: Content that may exist but is not described in detail or played on-screen.
safety_tools.x_card: A way for anyone to pause and remove or revise uncomfortable content without needing to justify the request.

cats.aim: What the group is trying to do during play.
cats.tone: The intended emotional and genre experience.
cats.safety: Boundaries and tools used to protect everyone.

players: Describe what their characters think, say, and do.
Ask questions about the scene before committing to action.
Choose how to pursue goals and accept that danger and complications move the story.
Manage Hope, Stress, Hit Points, Armor Slots, equipment, Experiences, and cards.
Contribute setting details when invited and help spotlight other players.
Narrate or co-narrate successes when appropriate.
game_master: Frame scenes and portray the world, NPCs, adversaries, and environments.
Tell players what their characters can easily perceive without requiring unnecessary rolls.
Call for a roll only when the outcome is uncertain and both success and failure are interesting.
Choose or approve the relevant trait and set Difficulty when a rule does not provide it.
State stakes, possible consequences, and unavoidable costs before the roll.
Use GM moves and Fear to keep events changing.
Move the spotlight fairly and maintain a safe, collaborative table.
shared_responsibility: Begin with the fiction, use mechanics, then return to the fiction.
Build on each other's ideas rather than protecting a prewritten outcome.
Make rulings that support the agreed tone and logic of the world.
Treat safety boundaries as living agreements that can be updated at any time.

known_limitations: This database does not replace exact card layout, character sheets, or the full Core Rulebook's examples and advice.
Some extracted SRD reference text may preserve minor typographic artifacts from the source PDF despite normalization.
The DPCGL can change; publication compliance must be checked again at redistribution time.
Hope & Fear is tracked as an upcoming expansion, not merged into the core rules.

validation_rules: JSON must parse with a standards-compliant parser.
Every catalog ID must be unique.
Every domain card must use one of the nine known domains and a level from 1 through 10.
Every class must reference exactly two known domains and two subclasses.
Every ancestry must expose its mechanical feature list.
Every community must expose one mechanical community feature.
Weapon tiers must be 1-4 and armor tiers must be 1-4.
Adversary and environment tiers must be 1-4.
Indexes must only reference IDs present in their corresponding catalog.
manual_normalization: Secondary weapon rows were reconstructed from the SRD table because the PDF's multi-column layout split several rows during table extraction.
Short explanatory summaries and implementation fields are original additions.
D&D template content was used only as a structural benchmark and was not merged as rules content.
